rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Thermoregulation maintains body temperature around 37°C (98.6°F).
Insulin lowers blood glucose; glucagon raises it.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Body temperature is maintained by shivering (heat production) and sweating (cooling).  ·  Glucose homeostasis involves insulin (lowers) and glucagon (raises) hormones.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Osmoregulation prevents dehydration by adjusting water intake and kidney function.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Explain how negative feedback maintains body temperature.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Positive feedback: amplification of a response (e.g., childbirth)  ·  Homeostatic variables: temperature, pH, glucose concentration, osmolarity

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ### 1. Homeostasis Overview  ·  - Homeostasis is the maintenance of stable internal conditions

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Homeostasis = stability through negative feedback loops.  ·  Set point = normal value that the system tries to maintain.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: What are the roles of insulin and glucagon in glucose regulation?  ·  How does the kidneys contribute to fluid and electrolyte homeostasis?

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Differentiate between acute (rapid) and chronic (long-term) responses.  ·  Understand the roles of the hypothalamus (temperature, hunger, thirst), pituitary, and adrenal glands.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Regulatory centers: hypothalamus, pituitary gland, endocrine glands

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Homeostasis relies on sensor organs detecting changes and control centers responding.  ·  Feedback loops are essential for maintaining stable internal environments.  ·  Multiple systems work together (e.g., nervous, endocrine, muscular) to achieve homeostasis.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: Describe the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis and its stress response.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: What is homeostasis? → A  ·  What is negative feedback? → B

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: - It involves negative feedback loops to counteract deviations from set points  ·  - Examples: temperature regulation, pH balance, glucose levels, fluid volume

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: The kidneys regulate fluid balance and electrolyte concentrations.  ·  Sensors detect changes, control centers respond, effectors implement changes.
